function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization that gives a person or entity the power to act on behalf of another party. Think of it as a “letter of authority” that tells a bank, broker, or service provider what they’re allowed to do. ### Key points | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Legal/Contractual basis** | A written agreement (often signed) that specifies the scope of authority. | | **Who can issue it** | Usually a client (the principal) who wants someone else (the agent) to perform tasks for them. | | **Typical uses** | • Banking – authorizing a bank to debit or credit accounts.
• Investment – giving a broker permission to trade on your behalf.
• Service providers – allowing a company to access data or systems. | | **Status categories** | • **Active** – currently valid and enforceable.
• **Pending** – awaiting approval or activation.
• **Inactive** – expired, revoked, or not yet activated. | ### Example in banking 1. **Client signs a mandate** giving a bank permission to automatically transfer money from their checking account to pay a utility bill each month. 2. The bank holds this mandate as an *active* record. 3. If the client cancels the mandate, it becomes *inactive*. 4. If the client has not yet approved the mandate, it’s *pending*. Mandates are essential for ensuring that only authorized parties can perform actions on someone’s behalf, providing both legal protection and operational clarity.
